_doc: Blood feuds and blood money (systems/bloodFeuds.js). A killing makes the dead one's kin owe vengeance on the killer's family: townsfolk families (a surname in a town), rival Houses, a realm's ruling line, and the player's own House. State on world.bloodFeuds (saved). A feud is { sides: [A, B], owes: the side with unavenged dead, heat 0..100, deaths, gens }. Heat cools by coolPerYear (× the realm's bloodPrice law cool) and flares on every new killing; a feud cooled below fadeBelow is forgotten. When the one who carries it (the eldest grown kinsman, a House's head, the player's House at a succession) dies or passes it on, the next takes it up at inherit.share of the heat (generations). Daily on its own hash rolls (no shared dice).
_kinds: How a death of each kind lights a feud (the kinds the townsfolk's memory keeps, systems/npcMemory.js, and the hooks' own). heat: the heat it adds. unjust: a lawful death (a hanging) — the share of families who still deem it unjust and swear vengeance (an innocent always does). by: who did it, for the annals.

stocks_died.label: left to die in the stocks

combat.label: killed in a trial by combat

battle.label: slain in a fight on the road

selfDefence.label: killed when they struck at their foe

_ranks: Wergild tariffs (gold) by the dead one's rank: a townsperson by role (child, beggar: low), a rival House's head or kin, a realm's ruler or royal kin. npcShare: what one family of townsfolk asks another (their purses are small).

wergild._doc: A blood price offered for the unavenged dead: the sum of their tariffs × the realm's bloodPrice law tariff × (1 + heat/heatDiv) × genShare^generations. Accepted on a hash roll: base + perDiplomacy × diplomacy + the law's accept − perHeat × heat (clamped). The coin goes to the bereaved's real purse (the eldest kinsman's, a House's gold, a crown's treasury); the arbiter's fee (feeShare) to the arbiter the law names: the town's council and priest (the town's purse), or the crown (the treasury). Refused: heat +refuseHeat, cooldown days before another offer.

marriage._doc: A match between the families ends the feud: your grown or young child promised into the other House (systems/betrothals.js, the asking price × askShare — they take less to end the blood); townsfolk wed one of each family (Townsfolk._wed, ages minAge..maxAge).

wipe._doc: The last of a family killed by your hand: the feud ends in the worst way. butcher: infamy (systems/atrocities.js), karma, reputation in their realm, the town's grief (an atrocity mark).

acts._doc: What avengers do against the player's House, a month at a time. A feud acts with chance heat/perHeatDiv a month; at most one act every gapDays across all feuds, and blows (waylay on the road, a knife in town) need heat ≥ blowAt, at most one every blowGapDays. A blow is struck on base − defence (martial skill, men under arms, companions), clamped; struck: a wound and health lost, the heat sated by sate; foiled: the avenger driven off, now and then (slainChance) killed in your defence (a selfDefence death: the feud flares). refuseAt: the family will not trade with you (systems/npcDisposition.js). testifyAt: they stand witness at your trial in their town (player/trials.js odds, perWitness each, at most maxWitnesses). hireAt: with heat this high the family's bitterest hires a blade — a sworn nemesis (systems/nemesis.js) once per feud. slander: reputation lost in their realm. A rival House carrying a blood feud keeps its feud with you at no less than houseFloor × heat (its own waylaying and plots act on it).

npc._doc: Feuds among the world's own: townsfolk families, rival Houses, a townsfolk family against a House whose men killed their kin. Each month: an avenger strikes with chance heat × killPerHeat (heat ≥ killAt; one killing per feud every feudKillGap days and one in the world every worldKillGap days — the cap that keeps it from a bloodbath); each year the feud may be settled (settleBase × (1 − heat/100), the town's council or a priest arbitrating: wergild from the killers' purses to the bereaved's, fee feeShare to the town; or a wedding between the families, marryShare of settlements). New feuds: brawls that end in a death, a hot street grudge (Brawls heat ≥ grudgeAt) turning to blood (grudgeChance a year across the world), rival Houses whose regard is at houseTieAt or below (houseChance a year).

text.inheritedYou: The blood feud with the {other} passes to {ruler}, a generation cooler.
text.letGo: The {side} let the old feud with the {other} lie.
text.faded: The feud between the {a} and the {b} is forgotten.

text.married: {x} of the {a} weds {y} of the {b}, and the feud ends at the altar.
text.marriedYou: {child} is promised to {who} of {house}, and the blood feud ends with the match.
text.wiped: The last of the {side} is dead by your hand. The feud is over: there is no one left to carry it. Folk cross themselves when your name is spoken.

text.blowSlain: {bearer} of the {side} came at you {where} and died on your blade. The feud burns hotter.
text.slander: The {side} speak of {dead}'s blood on your hands in {realm}.
